post.title: From Admission to Discharge: How Healthray Runs the Floor at Rainbow Hospital
post.excerpt: Rainbow Super Speciality Hospital runs 100 beds and 25 specialities in Vapi, with 50+ doctors on the floor. In 5+ years, it has grown into the kind of hospital where one patient can be admitted, operated on and discharged under a single roof.

fields.hero_lede: Rainbow Super Speciality Hospital runs 100 beds and 25 specialities in Vapi, with 50+ doctors on the floor. In 5+ years, it has grown into the kind of hospital where one patient can be admitted, operated on and discharged under a single roof.

glance_facts.label: Location
glance_facts.value: CM 8/16, NH 48, next to Nexa Showroom & Aakar Motors, Vapi, Gujarat

fields.overview_heading: How a Day Runs at Rainbow Hospital
overview_content: A busy day moves through four hands – the admission desk, the operating theatre, the billing counter and the records room. Each one holds the next. When a bed opens late or a file goes missing, every hand down the line waits with it.

That coordination was being done on phone calls, whiteboards and paper files. It held while volumes were small, but at this scale the gaps started to cost beds, theatre hours and staff time the hospital could not spare.
fields.problem_heading: Where the Floor Was Getting Stuck
fields.problem_intro: Four daily workflows were quietly draining capacity.

problems.title: Admissions
problems.text: With no live view of free, cleaned beds, placing a patient meant a ward-by-ward hunt that dragged on long after the call to admit.

problems.title: Operation Theatres
problems.text: Theatre lists were juggled by hand between surgeons. Starts slipped, and no one could see the idle gaps a case could have filled.

problems.title: Discharge & Claims
problems.text: A ready patient still waited while the summary and TPA file were built by hand and that occupied bed stayed shut to the next admission.

problems.title: Scattered Records
problems.text: One patient's history sat across unlinked files, so a specialist often re-ordered a test rather than hunt down a result that already existed.

fields.decision_intro: A senior clinician described the floor after go-live.
fields.quote_text: I used to piece a patient's history together from paper before I could even start. Now the past visits, scans and notes are already on the screen when she walks in – I spend the time on her, not on the file.
fields.solution_intro: The same four workflows now share one live system.

solutions.title: Live Bed Board
solutions.text: Every bed's status shows on one screen, so the desk assigns without a single call.

solutions.title: OT Planner
solutions.text: Surgeons book into a shared theatre calendar that exposes idle gaps to fill.

solutions.title: Claim-Ready Discharge
solutions.text: The summary and TPA file build as care is given, so the bill is ready at discharge.

solutions.title: One Patient Record
solutions.text: Every test, note and scan lands in one file the next doctor opens instantly.

fields.setup_intro: Healthray's team worked through three steps with the hospital before go-live.

steps.title: Workflows Mapped
steps.text: Healthray traced how beds, theatres and billing actually move, then shaped each module to it.

steps.title: Records Moved
steps.text: Existing patient histories were brought across so every ward opened with its records in place.

steps.title: Teams Trained
steps.text: Training ran by role, so ward, theatre and billing staff each practised their own screens.

fields.results_intro: Rainbow Hospital tracked these in the months after go-live.

results.title: Admissions Without the Hunt
results.text: A glance at the board shows which beds are free and ready, so an inpatient is placed in minutes, not a ward-by-ward search.

results.title: Beds Freed a Day Sooner
results.text: With the bill built on discharge day, the six-hour wait fell to three, and each freed bed opened to the next admission.

results.title: Theatres Run Fuller
results.text: Once idle gaps were visible, surgeons filled them, lifting OT use to about 90% and fitting more cases into the same day.

results.title: Claims Close in a Day
results.text: A TPA cycle that used to run three days now closes in one, pulling revenue closer to the date care was actually given.
